title: Krylov-Lie Algebras for Variational Quantum Algorithms: Geometric, Depth-Aware Insights into Expressivity and Trainability
summary: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are a leading approach to near-term quantum computation, but their utility is limited by barren plateaus and other pathologies in their loss landscapes. Existing landscape theories based on dynamical Lie algebras, Jordan-algebraic Wishart systems, approximate t-designs, and Haar-random circuits are foundational, but they often neglect the finite-depth geometry of realistic ansätze and are therefore ill-suited to the shallow-depth regime, where VQAs are poor approximators of 2-designs and trainability is most feasible.
